segments.t: Furious and pacing inside her dressing room trailer, iconic actress Beatrice Dalle vows never to return to the set. When Andrea explains that a lawsuit could ruin the agency, Beatrice fears she is being abandoned. Let's listen to their intense conversation in French first.
Je pense toujours à ce réalisateur Birag.
Cette histoire me met vraiment les nerfs!
Mais nous devons retourner sur le plateau.
Non, je n'y retournerai pas du tout.
Ils peuvent me faire un grand procès!
Je n'ai rien, je ne suis pas solvable.
Béatrice, les amendes vont retomber sur ASK.
Est-ce que tu es sérieuse, Andréa?
Notre agence est responsable des contrats signés.
Alors, est-ce que tu me lâches?
Non Béatrice, je ne te lâche jamais!
Je suis toujours à fond derrière toi.
Nous allons trouver une solution ensemble aujourd'hui.
D'accord, je te fais entièrement confiance, Andréa.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Je pense toujours à ce réalisateur Birag.
'I think constantly about this director Birag.' Beatrice fumes over her director's deception. The adverb 'toujours' indicates continuous thought.
Cette histoire me met vraiment les nerfs!
'This situation really gets on my nerves!' Beatrice vents her boiling irritation. The colloquial phrase 'the' conveys deep agitation.
Mais nous devons retourner sur le plateau.
'But we must return to the set.' Andrea gently reminds her of contractual reality. The noun 'film set' refers to a film set or soundstage.
Non, je n'y retournerai pas du tout.
'No, I will not return at all.' Beatrice digs in her heels stubbornly. The adverbial pronoun 'y' refers back to the film set.
Ils peuvent me faire un grand procès!
'They can bring a big lawsuit against me!' Beatrice dares the producers to sue her. The masculine noun 'lawsuit' means legal trial or lawsuit.
Je n'ai rien, je ne suis pas solvable.
'I have nothing, I am not solvent.' Beatrice points out she has no assets to seize. The financial adjective 'solvent' means solvent.
Béatrice, les amendes vont retomber sur ASK.
'Beatrice, the fines will fall back on ASK.' Andrea explains the harsh economic fallout for the agency. The verb 'to fall back' means to fall back on.
Est-ce que tu es sérieuse, Andréa?
'Are you serious, Andrea?' Beatrice is stunned by the collective exposure. The feminine adjective 'serious' questions authenticity.
Notre agence est responsable des contrats signés.
'Our agency is liable for signed contracts.' Andrea details their professional obligations. The adjective 'liable' denotes legal liability.
Alors, est-ce que tu me lâches?
'So, are you abandoning me?' Beatrice asks out of sudden vulnerability. The verb 'are abandoning' colloquially means to let down or abandon.
Non Béatrice, je ne te lâche jamais!
'No Beatrice, I never abandon you!' Andrea fiercely reassures her iconic client. The negative adverb 'ever' promises lifelong loyalty.
Je suis toujours à fond derrière toi.
'I am always completely behind you.' Andrea affirms total solidarity. The idiom 'a fond' means wholeheartedly or all the way.
Nous allons trouver une solution ensemble aujourd'hui.
'We are going to find a solution together today.' Andrea pivots constructively toward a resolution. The noun 'answer' means resolution or answer.
D'accord, je te fais entièrement confiance, Andréa.

'Alright, I trust you completely, Andrea.' Beatrice relents and places her faith in Andrea. The phrase 'place' means to trust. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.

Andrea reaffirms the deep bond of trust that connects an agent with an artist. By promising unwavering support, she restores Beatrice's morale while searching for a way out of the legal trap. Now let's listen to the scene once more.
